message:
a136/a137: the clamp ported to v2 and v1 — and it does NOT replace the backstop sweep

RETRACTION FIRST. a135 shipped with the claim that the ordering inequality is
what A21, A41, A43, A112, the backstop sweep and the -0.004 push-back all exist
to find, so "it now can't exist" and the sweep could go. That was wrong, and
REPLY02's "delete the sweep and bank 60 s" would have been a regression.

a136 — a mode probe first, because the payoff was assumed rather than measured:
  quick  clamp fires (7401 texels); backstop sweep NEVER REACHED
  v2     neither the clamp nor the sweep — the SHIPPED DEFAULT had no
         ordering protection at all
  v1     sweep runs: 63465 ms on troll, 12627 plate texels flattened; no clamp
So the invariant and the expensive search for its violations were in different
modes, and the default had neither. The 60 s is v1-only, and v1 has been
UI-disabled since a129 — banking it is bookkeeping on a disabled path.

Ported the clamp to v2 (bgBuildFullPlanesCore, against the layer's own visible
depth, on claimed texels only). Result, troll:
  a136 ordering clamp L0/bin1..10: 0 of 2,536,839 claimed texels were strictly
  in front of the surface they back.
v2 satisfies the invariant BY CONSTRUCTION — its per-bin depth is the source
field restricted to the bin, so a claimed texel cannot be nearer than what is
visible there. That is why v2 needs no protrusion apparatus and measures 0.00%
black at the user's poses. The clamp stays as a cheap standing assertion.

The v2 log is UNCONDITIONAL. The first version only printed on a violation, so
a clean v2 bake printed nothing — indistinguishable from the clamp not being
reached. That is a134's ambiguity one level down: an absent line is not
evidence of a clean pass.

a137 — the cross-validation, and the negative result. v1 is the only path
running both the clamp and the sweep, and the sweep shares no code with it:
it renders four extreme poses and back-projects on-screen protrusions.

  clamp OFF + sweep:  sweep flattened 12627 plate texels (66821 ms)
  clamp ON  + sweep:  clamp found 0 same-texel violations
                      sweep still flattened 12604 (67255 ms)

0.2% difference. The clamp is a SAME-TEXEL invariant; the sweep searches
REPROJECTED poses, where the plate and the FG occluding it have parallaxed to
different screen positions, so "the surface it backs" at a pose is not dQ at
the same index. brief §4.4's formula, read literally, is a same-texel statement
and does not retire the sweep. The two guard different populations.

The harness comment predicted exactly this residue before the run and said what
it would mean; that is what happened.

What a135 still earns on its own merits, unchanged: in QUICK it removed 7401
texels (0.85%) strictly in front of the surface at their own index, worst 86 px
of misplacement at the rim, with black% and comb both slightly better. Kept.

Also measured: v1 bake 118952 ms with the sweep, 45535 ms without — the sweep is
62% of v1's bake, and v1 is 4x quick either way.

regress.js masks: ALL PASS (8).
